open_points.subject: First-administrator bootstrap audit timestamp
open_points.text: A28 says “the bootstrap, which builds its own audit, keeps its one instant,” but M37 says “audit_writer supplies audit_id and occurred_at; callers cannot supply either.”
open_points.question: Does the bootstrap bypass the audit writer and set its audit record’s occurred_at to the bootstrap operation’s single clock instant, or must it use the audit writer, which takes occurred_at when appending?
options: Bootstrap constructs/appends its audit with occurred_at equal to the account creation instant, as an explicit exception to M37.
Bootstrap sends an AuditIntent through audit_writer, whose separate clock read determines occurred_at.
Bootstrap uses audit_writer but the writer accepts the bootstrap instant, contradicting the rule that the writer takes occurred_at itself.
open_points.default_guess: Treat bootstrap as an explicit exception to M37: its audit occurred_at equals the single bootstrap instant; another mechanism supplies audit_id.

witness.initial: The staff table is empty; the clock can advance between creation of the first administrator and insertion of its audit record.
events: The host operator runs the bootstrap command.
Bootstrap reads instant T1 and creates the active verified administrator.
The audit is appended after the clock has advanced to T2.
outcomes: Following A28’s bootstrap clause, the account timestamps and audit occurred_at are all T1.
Following M37, bootstrap passes an AuditIntent to audit_writer and the audit occurred_at is T2.
witness.observer: A persistence-level test or operator inspecting the staff and audit rows sees whether the bootstrap audit time equals the account creation time.
